current_manifest_row.title: Absolute convergence and tail bound for bounded discounted rewards
current_manifest_row.statement:
Let $M\ge0$, $0\le\gamma<1$, and let $(\rho_j)_{j\ge1}$ be any real sequence with $|\rho_j|\le M$. Then the series

$$ \sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\gamma^j\rho_{j+1} $$

converges absolutely; write $G$ for its sum. Every partial sum and the limit satisfy

$$ \left|\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\gamma^j\rho_{j+1}\right|\le\frac{M}{1-\gamma}, \qquad |G|\le\frac{M}{1-\gamma}. $$

For every integer $N\ge0$,

$$ \left|G-\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\gamma^j\rho_{j+1}\right|\le\frac{M\gamma^N}{1-\gamma}, $$

where the partial sum at $N=0$ is empty and $\gamma^0=1$, including when $\gamma=0$.
current_manifest_row.strategy: Compare the absolute reward terms with the geometric series, then pass the finite geometric tail bound to the limit.

current_manifest_row.title: A unit reward on a self-loop has no finite undiscounted return
current_manifest_row.statement: Take the finite MDP with $S=\{s\}$, $A(s)=\{a\}$, reward alphabet $\mathcal R=\{1\}$, and $p(s,1\mid s,a)=1$. current_manifest_row.title: Finite-MDP Bellman operators are gamma contractions with unique fixed points
current_manifest_row.statement:
Let a finite MDP and a discount $0\le\gamma<1$ be fixed. For $U\in\mathbb R^S$, define $\|U\|_\infty=0$ if $S=\emptyset$, and $\|U\|_\infty=\max_{s\in S}|U(s)|$ otherwise. For every stationary policy $\pi$ and all $V,W\in\mathbb R^S$,

$$ \|T^\pi V-T^\pi W\|_\infty\le\gamma\|V-W\|_\infty. $$

The Bellman optimality operator satisfies the same inequality. Each of $T^\pi$ and $T^*$ has exactly one fixed point in $\mathbb R^S$. The contraction constant is the nonnegative number $\gamma$.
current_manifest_row.strategy: Bound the finite probability-weighted averages and finite maxima in sup norm, then apply Banach with q=γ on the complete finite-state value space.

current_manifest_row.title: Exact finite policy iteration with retained greedy actions
current_manifest_row.statement:
Input a finite MDP, a discount $0\le\gamma<1$, an initial deterministic policy $\pi_0$, and, for each state $s$, an ordered list containing each member of $A(s)$ exactly once. For $k=0,1,\ldots$:

1. Associate to each deterministic policy $\pi_k$ the stationary Markov policy $\widehat\pi_k(a\mid s)=1$ if $a=\pi_k(s)$ and $0$ otherwise. Compute the unique exact policy evaluation $V_k\in\mathbb R^S$ satisfying $T^{\widehat\pi_k}V_k=V_k$.
2. For each $s$, set

$$ Q_k(s,a)=r(s,a)+\gamma\sum_{s'\in S}P(s'\mid s,a)V_k(s'). $$

If $\pi_k(s)$ attains $\max_{a\in A(s)}Q_k(s,a)$, set $\pi_{k+1}(s)=\pi_k(s)$. Otherwise set $\pi_{k+1}(s)$ to the earliest maximizing action in the supplied list.
3. If $\pi_{k+1}=\pi_k$, return $(\pi_k,V_k)$. Otherwise continue with $\pi_{k+1}$.

The operator fixed point used for exact policy evaluation exists and is unique by the finite-MDP contraction theorem.
current_manifest_row.strategy: Define exact policy evaluation, deterministic greedy improvement using a supplied action list, tie retention, and the stop condition.

current_manifest_row.title: Expected discounted policy value is a fixed point of its Bellman operator
current_manifest_row.statement:
For a finite MDP, a discount $0\le\gamma<1$, and any stationary Markov policy $\pi$, the expected discounted state value defined from each initial state satisfies

$$ T^\pi V^\pi=V^\pi. $$

If $S=\emptyset$, this is the equality of the unique empty functions and no choice axiom is needed. If $S\ne\emptyset$, assume the Axiom of Choice for the path-law definition of $V^\pi$.

current_manifest_row.title: A common reward shift moves every one-state Bellman value equally
current_manifest_row.statement: Let $S=\{s\}$, $A(s)=\{a,b\}$, and $\gamma=1/2$. Both actions return deterministically to $s$, with reward $1$ under $a$ and reward $3$ under $b$. View the deterministic policies choosing $a$ and $b$ as stationary policies assigning probability one to those actions; their unique policy Bellman fixed points are $2$ and $6$, respectively. More generally, for a stationary policy with $\theta:=\pi(b\mid s)\in[0,1]$, its fixed point is $2+4\theta$. After adding $2$ to both rewards, the deterministic-policy fixed points are $6$ and $10$, and the fixed point for the same stochastic policy is $6+4\theta$. Thus every policy value shifts by $2/(1-\gamma)=4$, the difference between the two deterministic-policy values remains $4$, and $b$ maximizes the Bellman optimality backup at the optimal fixed point in both models.
current_manifest_row.strategy: Evaluate the two geometric discounted returns before and after the common reward shift.

current_manifest_row.title: Greedy policy improvement and finite policy-iteration termination
current_manifest_row.statement:
Let a finite MDP and $0\le\gamma<1$ be fixed, and let $V^*$ denote the unique fixed point of $T^*$. If $S=\emptyset$, the statewise claims below are vacuous and the policy iteration procedure returns the unique empty policy after one evaluation, without Choice. If $S\ne\emptyset$, assume the Axiom of Choice. For a stationary policy $\pi$, let $V^\pi$ be its expected discounted state value. For a deterministic policy $\sigma$, define its associated stationary policy by $\widehat\sigma(a\mid s)=1$ if $a=\sigma(s)$ and $0$ otherwise, and interpret $T^\sigma$ and $V^\sigma$ as $T^{\widehat\sigma}$ and $V^{\widehat\sigma}$.

$$ Q_V(s,a)=r(s,a)+\gamma\sum_{s'\in S}P(s'\mid s,a)V(s'). $$

If a deterministic policy $\pi'$ chooses an action maximizing $Q_{V^\pi}(s,a)$ at every state, then $V^{\pi'}(s)\ge V^\pi(s)$ for every $s$. If $(T^{\pi'}V^\pi)(s)>V^\pi(s)$ at any state, the value inequality is strict at some state.

For exact finite policy iteration, supply an initial deterministic policy and a finite ordered list of the actions at each state; evaluate each policy at its exact Bellman fixed point; retain the current action whenever it is already greedy; otherwise choose the earliest maximizing action in the supplied list. Every changed policy then strictly improves the value at some state and weakly improves it at every state. The procedure makes at most $N_{\rm det}-1$ changes, where $N_{\rm det}$ is the finite number of deterministic policies, and terminates at a deterministic policy whose value is $V^*$; this value dominates the value of every stationary policy.
current_manifest_row.strategy: Use the Bellman fixed-point identities, monotonicity of positive probability averages, contraction iteration, and finiteness of deterministic policies; retain the current action at every tie.

current_manifest_row.title: Extended value iteration for a confidence set
current_manifest_row.statement:
Input finite nonempty state and action sets, upper reward estimates $\widetilde r(s,a)$, empirical transition laws $\widehat P(\cdot\mid s,a)$, nonnegative transition radii $b_p(s,a)$, a tolerance $\varepsilon>0$, and fixed orders of the states and actions for tie-breaking. For a vector $v\in\mathbb R^S$, write $\operatorname{span}(v)=\max_s v(s)-\min_s v(s)$ and let $\Delta(S)$ be the probability simplex on $S$. Initialize $u_0(s)=0$. At iteration $i\ge1$, compute
$$u_i(s)=\max_{a\in A(s)}\left[\widetilde r(s,a)+\max_{q\in\Delta(S):\|q-\widehat P(\cdot\mid s,a)\|_1\le b_p(s,a)}q\cdot u_{i-1}\right].$$
For every state-action pair $(s,a)$, compute a maximizing transition vector as follows, using $v=u_{i-1}$. Put $q=\widehat P(\cdot\mid s,a)$, $c=\min\{1,b_p(s,a)/2\}$, and order the states $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ by nondecreasing $v(x_j)$, using the fixed state order to break ties. Set $j=1$ and $\ell=m$. While $c>0$ and $j<\ell$, advance $j$ while $q(x_j)=0$, then decrease $\ell$ while $j<\ell$ and $q(x_\ell)=1$. If $j\ge\ell$, stop. If $v(x_j)\ge v(x_\ell)$, stop. Otherwise set $d=\min\{c,q(x_j),1-q(x_\ell)\}$, replace $q(x_j)$ by $q(x_j)-d$ and $q(x_\ell)$ by $q(x_\ell)+d$, and replace $c$ by $c-d$; repeat. Each positive transfer either uses all remaining mass or exhausts a source coordinate or fills a destination coordinate, so the loop takes at most $2m+1$ positive transfers. It moves at most $b_p(s,a)/2$ mass, hence the resulting vector is feasible. Any feasible vector redistributes at most this much mass from coordinates it decreases to coordinates it increases. Pairing the least-valued available source with the greatest-valued available destination first maximizes the linear gain; the procedure continues exactly while such a pair has positive gain and capacity. Thus the resulting $q_{i,s,a}$ maximizes $q\cdot u_{i-1}$ over the stated confidence set. The inner maximum exists because each nonempty feasible subset of $\Delta(S)$ is compact.

For each state, compute $B_i(s,a)=\widetilde r(s,a)+q_{i,s,a}\cdot u_{i-1}$ for every action, record the first action $a_i(s)$ in the fixed action order attaining $\max_{a\in A(s)}B_i(s,a)$, and set $q_i(\cdot\mid s)=q_{i,s,a_i(s)}$. If $\operatorname{span}(u_i-u_{i-1})<\varepsilon$, return the stationary deterministic policy $\pi_i(s)=a_i(s)$, its corresponding maximizing transition rows $q_i$, the vector $u_{i-1}$ used in that backup, and the iteration index. The finite sort-and-fill operations and fixed tie rules make the returned quantities measurable functions of the estimates. Otherwise continue. The algorithm is a partial procedure unless a separate termination result is established.
current_manifest_row.strategy: State the exact finite-state model, conventions, and hypotheses; justify the stated conclusion from the cited interfaces.

current_manifest_row.title: UCRL2 for finite communicating MDPs
current_manifest_row.statement:
The learner is given a finite nonempty state set $\mathcal S$, a finite nonempty action set $A(s)$ for each $s\in\mathcal S$, the observed initial state $s_1\in\mathcal S$, a horizon $T\ge1$, a confidence parameter $\delta\in(0,1)$, and fixed orders of the states and each state's actions. Let $S=|\mathcal S|$ and $A=\max_{s\in\mathcal S}|A(s)|$. Its unknown environment is a finite communicating MDP on $\mathcal S$ and these action sets with rewards in $[0,1]$; the transition kernel, reward laws, and their means are not inputs to the learner. At interaction $t$, the learner observes the current state $S_t$, chooses an admissible action, and then observes the realized reward $\rho_t$ and next state $S_{t+1}$.

Initialize $t=1$ and $S_1=s_1$. At the start $t_k$ of episode $k$, let $N_k(s,a)$ be the total number of visits to $(s,a)$ before $t_k$. If $N_k(s,a)>0$, let $\widehat r_k(s,a)$ be the mean of the rewards observed on those visits and $\widehat P_k(\cdot\mid s,a)$ their empirical next-state law. If $N_k(s,a)=0$, set $\widehat r_k(s,a)=0$ and set $\widehat P_k(\cdot\mid s,a)$ to the point mass at the first state in the fixed state order. Put $n_k(s,a)=\max\{1,N_k(s,a)\}$ and
$$b^r_k(s,a)=\sqrt{\frac{7\log(2SAt_k/\delta)}{2n_k(s,a)}},\qquad b^p_k(s,a)=\sqrt{\frac{14S\log(2At_k/\delta)}{n_k(s,a)}}.$$
Set $\widetilde r_k(s,a)=\min\{1,\widehat r_k(s,a)+b^r_k(s,a)\}$. Run extended value iteration with these estimates/radii and tolerance $1/\sqrt{t_k}$, obtaining a stationary deterministic policy $\pi_k$. Set every within-episode count $v_k(s,a)=0$ and execute the following loop. While $t\le T$, observe $S_t$, choose $a_t=\pi_k(S_t)$, observe $\rho_t$ and $S_{t+1}$, increment $v_k(S_t,a_t)$ and the all-history count for $(S_t,a_t)$, record this reward/transition observation, and retain the observed next state as the current state for the next interaction. Increment $t$ by one. End the episode immediately after an interaction when its pair's count reaches $v_k(s,a)=\max\{1,N_k(s,a)\}$, where $N_k$ remains the episode-start count; if $t\le T$, begin the next episode, otherwise terminate. All action and transition-vector ties use the fixed orders. The positive radii ensure finite inner termination by the separate termination lemma. In particular, always $v_k(s,a)\le\max\{1,N_k(s,a)\}$; when $N_k(s,a)>0$, a completed triggering episode doubles that pair's total count.

current_manifest_row.title: Termination of extended value iteration under communicating assumptions
current_manifest_row.statement:
For every finite nonempty state/action system, bounded real upper rewards, probability-vector empirical centers, strictly positive transition radii, and tolerance $\varepsilon>0$, extended value iteration terminates. More precisely, write $F$ for its optimistic Bellman operator, put $\eta=\min_{s,a}\min\{1,b_p(s,a)/2\}>0$, and set $u_0=0$, $u_i=F(u_{i-1})$. Then
$$\operatorname{span}(u_i-u_{i-1})\le(1-\eta)^{i-1}\operatorname{span}(u_1),\qquad i\ge1.$$
When $\eta=1$, the span is zero for $i\ge2$. In particular, the positive UCRL2 confidence radii give finite stopping with tolerance $1/\sqrt{t_k}$ in every episode of a finite communicating MDP, including episodes whose confidence set misses the true model.
current_manifest_row.strategy: Decompose each positive L1 ball into a common positive mass and a residual subprobability; prove a span contraction and geometric decay.

current_manifest_row.title: UCRL2 high-probability pathwise regret bound
current_manifest_row.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice for the path-law and martingale suppliers. Let a finite communicating MDP have $S\ge1$ states, at most $A\ge1$ actions per state, rewards in $[0,1]$, and normalized diameter $D$. For each initial state, integer horizon $T\ge2$, and $\delta\in(0,1)$, UCRL2 with confidence parameter $\delta$ satisfies
$$\Pr\!\left(\Delta_T\le34DS\sqrt{AT\log(T/\delta)}\right)\ge1-\delta.$$
For every integer $T\ge1$, the same algorithm also satisfies
$$\Pr\!\left(\Delta_T\le34DS\sqrt{AT\log(2T/\delta)}\right)\ge1-\delta.$$
Here $\Delta_T=T\rho^*-R_T$ is realized, pathwise regret and logarithms are natural. These are assertions for each fixed horizon and initial state. The original formula with $\log(T/\delta)$ and $T\ge1$ is false, as refuted below.
current_manifest_row.strategy: Use fixed-tape anytime confidence, the local EVI contraction, finite-horizon span control, predictable martingale increments, count doubling, and explicit constants; refute the exact original T=1 formula.
